subject: Demo follow-up: HealthBridge Labs - prompt/output PII handling & retention alignment
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Palmer <susan.palmer@healthbridgelabs.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention (HealthBridge)

Hi Susan — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups we promised to clarifying around PII and prompt/output handling so your security and infra teams can validate.

Recap high level: HealthBridge liked our latency and the canary rollback plan; the main security asks were about what exactly Redwood persists from prompts and generated outputs, where that data is stored (region), and how long logs/trace data are retained.

Can you confirm the list of fields you consider PII for this use case? During the call you mentioned patient name, MRN (medical record number), and insurance IDs — is that exhaustive or are there other sensitive fields we should treat as PII (e.g., free-text clinical notes with embedded identifiers, phone numbers, SSNs)?

Specifically we want to confirm the following items and will respond with concrete options for each:
- Allowed telemetry for hosted evaluation vs. production (can we enable DEBUG logs for initial integration?)
- Prompt/output retention TTL you require (applies to stored request/response payloads)
- Whether HealthBridge requires data residency (US-only) for prompt payloads, logs, and backups
- Need for audit trail / access logs for every time a human views or a support engineer retrieves a prompt/output sample
- Whether KV cache persistence (for inference speed) must be disabled or kept in-memory only

If you prefer, we can prepare a short one-page statement on what Redwood will and will not persist for prompts/outputs for your legal/security review. Jordan will drop the technical appendix with the dataflow diagram and retention policy after this thread.

Next steps we propose:
1) You send back a short list of fields you consider PII (if different from the items above)
2) We share a written confirmation of defaults + options (ephemeral mode, per-route TTL, dedicated/private deployment behavior)
3) Schedule a 30-minute session with your infra lead to review KV cache and audit log mechanics (tentative: Thu 08/05)

Thanks — Hannah

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention (HealthBridge)

Hi Hannah — appreciate the follow-up and clear list. To answer your questions from our side:

Short list of fields we classify as PII for this integration (must be treated specially):
- Patient full name
- Medical Record Number (MRN)
- Insurance ID / Policy number
- Dates tied to identifiable care events (DOB is sensitive)
- Phone numbers and personal email addresses
- Any US SSNs or Tax IDs if present in free text
- Health insurance claims IDs

We also want to call out free-text clinical notes: if a prompt includes verbatim clinical notes that contain identifiers, we treat those as PII and require the same controls.

Retention/Residency/Logging asks:
- TTL: for anything classified as PII, HealthBridge requires a max retention of 30 days unless we explicitly sign an exception.
- Residency: our data must remain within US regions while processed and at-rest (we are not looking for EU residency on this project).
- Logging: we require an audit trail showing who accessed any stored prompt/output, with timestamps and job-ids. The audit trail itself can be stored for up to 365 days.
- KV cache: we prefer KV cache to be in-memory only with no persistent snapshots written to disk. If Redwood cannot guarantee that for hosted, we need to evaluate Dedicated or Private options.

Can you confirm whether your hosted evaluation environment will persist prompt/output payloads by default for 30 days? If so, we will ask for a written opt-out path for production or an option to enable ephemeral-only mode.

Also, please include a simple dataflow diagram that shows where request/response payloads, KV cache, and logs live for the hosted and dedicated options.

Thanks — Susan

Susan Palmer
Head of Product Security, HealthBridge Labs
susan.palmer@healthbridgelabs.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Palmer <susan.palmer@healthbridgelabs.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention (HealthBridge)

Hi Susan — Jordan here (Sales Engineer). Thanks for enumerating the PII fields — super helpful. Below is a concise technical mapping and explicit answers to your asks. I’ll attach the diagram and a short retention summary for legal.

1) Hosted evaluation default behaviour (what we do today):
- Prompt payloads and generated outputs are collected for debugging/quality by default and retained for 30 days. These logs are stored in the configured cloud region (we can pin to a US region).
- Access to stored prompt/output samples is restricted by role (engineer/support/admin scopes) and all access events are recorded in our audit logging system. You can request a daily audit export.
- KV cache used for inference acceleration is in-memory on GPU instances; Redwood does not persist KV cache to object storage under normal operation. We do have internal periodic checkpoints for stateful features in certain Dedicated builds — those are disabled for hosted by default and can be explicitly turned off.

2) Options we can offer to match your requirements:
- Ephemeral route mode: route-specific setting that disables retention of request/response payloads entirely (no prompt/output stored) — good for PII-heavy flows.
- Per-route TTL: set <30d TTL or 0 to prevent storage. For HealthBridge, we can set default TTL to 30d and make it configurable to 0d for specific routes that handle clinical notes.
- Residency: we can enforce US-only storage for both logs and persisted payloads for your org/project (we’ll show region pinning in the dataflow).
- Audit trail: we can surface audit logs showing who accessed a payload, with timestamp, role, and reason; retention for audit logs can be set to 365d.
- Dedicated / Private: if you require additional guarantees (no shared debugging collection, stricter KV cache controls), Dedicated or Private deployments are available; those can be configured to never checkpoint KV cache and to route all logs to your SIEM via secure connectors.

3) Encryption & key management:
- All persisted payloads are encrypted at rest. For Dedicated and Private, you may supply a customer-managed key (KMS/HSM) for additional control.

Attachments: I’ve attached a simplified dataflow diagram (redwood-dataflow-diagram.png) and a one-page retention policy summary (retention-policy-summary.pdf) for legal and infra review.

If this aligns with HealthBridge’s requirements, Hannah will draft a short written confirmation we can both sign off on before the pilot. Happy to run the infra call on Thu 08/05 — I’m available 10:00–12:00 PT.

— Jordan

Susan — thanks for the clarity and Jordan for the detailed technical mapping. Two quick asks to close this out so we can move the MDP pilot forward:

1) Can you confirm in reply that 30 days (for PII) and US-only residency are acceptable as the default for initial pilot, with route-level opt-out to set TTL=0 for PII-heavy endpoints? We’ll include the ephemeral route option in the MAP.
2) Please confirm whether HealthBridge wants the KV cache explicitly disabled in hosted tests, or if it’s acceptable to run with in-memory-only KV cache (no persistence or checkpoints). If you prefer disabled, we’ll mark that as required for pilot and discuss Dedicated options.

Assuming we get your confirmation, we’ll: (a) produce a one-page confirmation statement for legal, (b) lock the pilot scope (routes with TTL controls, US residency), and (c) schedule Thu 08/05 10:30 PT for infra review.

Best — Hannah
